subject: Geopolitics
title: The US-Mexico Border Wall
description: A micro-lesson that makes The US-Mexico Border Wall usable.

hook.text: The US–Mexico border stretches 3,145 km. Building a wall across it became America's most polarizing debate.

buildup.text: Supporters say walls control illegal immigration. Opponents say people find tunnels, ladders, and visa routes.

discovery.text: Border walls are as much symbols as structures. They signal political toughness, not just physical security.

twist.text: Most undocumented immigrants overstay legal visas. A wall can't stop someone who flew in on a plane.

climax.text: The wall debate reveals a deeper divide: how nations balance security, identity, and humanitarian duties.

punchline.text: Walls speak louder about fear than about policy.

quiz.question: How do most undocumented immigrants enter the US?
options: By crossing the southern border on foot
